capabilities.target: enrich.lookup paid enrichment API, billed per call against a shared monthly quota
Researcher sub-agent tasked with investigating an account
CRM account record fields (industry, size, headquarters)

inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows (40,000 rows/night, roughly 3 percent with malformed company names)

instructions.note: "Keep going until every row is complete" sets no bound on retries, spend, or sub-agent spawns, and runtime notes confirm roughly 3 percent of the 40,000 nightly rows can never complete, so this instruction guarantees indefinite retrying/spawning for those rows every night.
"looks incomplete" is not defined, leaving the model wide latitude to decide when to retry or spawn a researcher, with no criterion that would stop it on unresolvable rows.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota
Sales and marketing tools dependent on the shared enrichment quota

controls.name: Step, runtime, retry, and recursion-depth limit
controls.decay_rationale: A hard bound enforced by the orchestrator, not the model, would not depend on model behavior. None exists today per runtime notes.

controls.name: Spend cap on enrichment API usage
controls.decay_rationale: A budget enforced by the API gateway or billing platform would not depend on model behavior. None exists today.

controls.name: Spend and quota consumption alert
controls.decay_rationale: Alerting does not depend on model behavior, but is detective only and was explicitly stated as absent ("There is no spend alert on the enrichment account").

controls.name: Dead-letter handling for unresolvable rows
controls.decay_rationale: A structural cutoff that routes a row to review after N failed attempts would not depend on model behavior. None exists; the prompt instead says to keep retrying or spawning.

controls.name: Dedicated, scoped credential and quota for the enrichment agent
controls.decay_rationale: A quota scoped to this agent alone would sever the cross-team blast radius path independent of model behavior. The key is instead shared with sales and marketing.

findings.title: Unbounded retry and recursive sub-agent spawning on unresolvable rows drains a shared enrichment quota (TC6 spend loop)

attack_path.note: Nightly batch of 40,000 rows; roughly 3 percent (about 1,200 rows) have malformed company names that enrich.lookup can never resolve completely
Billed per call; prompt instructs retrying on failure or incomplete result with no attempt limit
No limit on sub-agent count or recursion depth; spawned researchers can spawn further researchers
Shared monthly quota; once exhausted it stays exhausted until the next month
Loses enrichment capability once the shared quota is exhausted

forecast.watch_signal: Track nightly spend against the shared quota, the maximum sub-agent recursion depth actually reached, and the count of rows still retrying past N attempts; any rise confirms the uncontrolled consumption pattern is active and would only worsen if the batch grows or new lookup tools are added.

evidence.observation: "If a lookup fails or looks incomplete, retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent to investigate the account. Keep going until every row is complete" sets no stopping condition.
"There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents. Sub agents can spawn their own researchers."

"Roughly 3 percent of rows have malformed company names that never return a complete result," which under the prompt's stopping rule guarantees perpetual retry and spawning for those rows every night.
"There is no spend alert on the enrichment account."

recommendations.action: Enforce a hard per-run cap on enrich.lookup calls, retries per row, and sub-agent spawn depth, enforced by the orchestrator rather than the prompt.
Route rows that still fail after N attempts to a dead-letter list for batch or human review instead of retrying or spawning indefinitely.
Add a real-time spend/quota-consumption alert for the enrichment key so an in-progress runaway run can be caught before the quota is exhausted.
Give the enrichment agent its own quota or sub-reservation, separate from sales and marketing, so a runaway run cannot degrade other teams' tooling.

findings.title: Shared enrichment credential couples this agent's failures to unrelated teams' service availability (ASI03 confused deputy)

attack_path.note: Operates under a credential whose quota is shared_service_account scope across this agent, sales, and marketing
Sales and marketing tools stop working until the next month once this agent exhausts the shared quota, even though they never authorized this agent's consumption

forecast.watch_signal: Watch for additional teams or services being added to the shared enrichment key, or any widening of this agent's credential scope, which would widen the blast radius further.

evidence.observation: "The API key and its monthly quota are shared with the sales and marketing teams; when the quota runs out, their tools stop working until the next month."

recommendations.action: Issue the enrichment agent a dedicated API key and quota, separate from sales and marketing, so a malfunction in this agent cannot exhaust a resource those teams depend on.
If a dedicated key cannot be issued immediately, set a hard sub-quota reservation for this agent within the shared key so it cannot consume the full monthly allowance.

rating.rationale: Two findings reach critical. F1: the prompt's unbounded retry-or-spawn instruction, combined with no step/runtime/retry/recursion limit and a deterministic subset (~3 percent) of rows that can never complete, produces a guaranteed nightly spend loop against a paid, shared-quota API (TC6), with A4 autonomy and unbounded sub-agent spawning applying the autonomy modifier. F2: that same quota is shared with sales and marketing, so the agent's own malfunction degrades tooling for teams that never authorized its use (ASI03 confused deputy). No declared or verified controls exist anywhere on these paths (all five relevant controls are missing_recommended), so residual equals inherent for both findings. Because the gap is architectural (absent caps and an unseparated credential) rather than something that decays with model capability, the forecast does not worsen under the triggers considered, but it also will not improve without the P1 recommendations: hard step/spend/recursion caps, a dead-letter path for unresolvable rows, and a dedicated quota for this agent.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP config, or sub-agent prompt was provided. Whether spawned researcher sub-agents inherit the same unbounded retry/spawn logic and the same shared credential is inferred from the parent prompt and runtime notes, not confirmed from the sub-agent's own instructions.

No information was provided on cap.crm_write's credential scope or on any validation step before writing enriched fields to the CRM, so that capability's credential_scope is recorded as unknown rather than assumed.
